newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N.chief sends condolences to Israel over crash.
newsitem.headline: U.N.chief sends condolences to Israel over crash.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan late on Tuesday sent condolences to Israel over the mid-air collision of two helicopters that claimed the lives of 73 Israeli soldiers.
In a statement, Annan said that he "learned with regret of the mid-air collision of two Israeli transport helicopters over northern Israel with the loss of over 70 lives."
He expressed "condolences to the government and people of Israel as well as to the bereaved families of the victims."

The collision of the two Sikorsky CH-53 transporters in northern Israel en route to southern Lebanon was the worst military aviation disaster in the nearly 50 years of Israeli history. The helicopters were flying to the occupation zone in southern Lebanon which Israel carved out in 1985 to repel guerrillas attacks.
